::: {.why}
Five weeks of machinery produce one weight vector today, and the point of the exercise is that every element of it traces back to something you measured rather than chose.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Produce a position vector for your combined book where each input is traceable to a measurement.
- State which single input the result is most sensitive to, and by how much.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Wire it together in qlib/portfolio.py: covariance from your chosen estimator, neutralisation against the exposures you decided to hedge, volatility targeting to your chosen level, scaled by your Kelly fraction, capped by leverage. Produce the weight vector and the predicted risk decomposition.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run the sensitivity: perturb each of the five inputs by a plausible amount, one at a time, and report the change in the resulting positions and in predicted risk. Name the input that dominates, which will almost certainly be the expected return estimate rather than anything in the risk model.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The full sizing pipeline runs end to end: covariance, neutralisation, volatility target, Kelly fraction, leverage cap. Phase 6 changes only what feeds it, and phase 10 runs this exact code on a schedule.
:::
